sources.description: Platform-free stage plate: the painting with platforms, floor bank and rings removed; generated pixels outside the removal masks discarded. The owner confirmed this platform-free version on 2026-11-13 (their copy is a lossy WebP of the same image; this lossless file is the source).
sources.tool: Codex built-in image editor (precise-object-edit), 2026-09-07; deterministic mask restore
sources.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: the supplied Verdant sanctuary master. Produce a gameplay-free environmental clean plate, keeping the exact camera, framing, tree silhouette, curved roots, arches, painterly texture, palette, light and all unaffected scenery unchanged. Remove ALL SIX flat floating moss-topped rectangular gameplay platforms: upper right, upper center, middle left, middle right, lower left, lower right. Completely remove their dark rectangular bodies, moss caps, hanging foliage and straight platform-specific reflections; naturally complete the forest, tree, architecture or water previously hidden behind each. Remove BOTH faint dashed yellow elliptical rings on the water near the bottom. Remove the straight moss-capped gameplay floor/bank spanning the bottom center (approximately x200 to1450 y824 to915 in this 1672x941 image), continuing the flooded water down behind it, while preserving the curved foreground tree roots and foliage on both sides. These removals are the ONLY changes. Do not remove genuine curved ruined arches or the majestic central tree. No platforms, no yellow rings, no horizontal gameplay floor, no actors, no HUD, no text. Return the same wide composition and resolution, not a reimagined scene.
sources.licence: Derived from the owner's master; owner-owned.

sources.description: 2440x1453 camera-support plate: the exact clean plate at (384,256) with a painted exterior for wide and tall cameras, joined by a harmonic gradient stitch (core unchanged).
sources.tool: Codex built-in image editor (outpainting), then deterministic harmonic gradient stitch with the core locked
sources.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit / outpainting. Asset: Tear Verdant sanctuary external overscan. Use the visible padded image immediately above as the exact edit target. Fill ONLY its solid magenta outside border with a seamless continuation of the same hand-painted flooded forest sanctuary. The 1672x941 central original occupies x=384..2055, y=256..1196 in a 2440x1453 canvas. Keep that entire rectangle unchanged, at exactly the same position, size, perspective, palette and lighting. Do not zoom, crop, move, resize, recolor or redesign the central tree, sun aperture, ruined arches, water, vines, roots or foliage. The final image should retain the full 2440x1453 padded composition. Extend dark dense canopy naturally across the top, layered dark forest and mossy rock vegetation to the sides, and low shadowed bank roots/foliage and water continuation below. Match details and boundary lines exactly at each edge of the locked rectangle so no rectangular seam is visible. The new borders should be subordinate peripheral scenery, not new focal landmarks. No new central trees, repeated/copy-pasted sanctuary, new hero ruins, floating platforms, traversable ledges, actors, enemies, weapons, glowing gameplay rings, UI, text, outlines, grids or watermarks. Remove all magenta by painting only the exterior. This is a scenery-only expanded camera support plate, not a new scene composition.

sources.description: Segmentation of the nearest framing trunks and root masses (1672x941, white = frame).
sources.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: registered grayscale occlusion mask for a layered 2D game background. Input image is the exact structural backing, 1672x941. Produce ONLY a black-and-white segmentation mask at identical framing and aspect ratio: WHITE for the two very nearest dark foreground side tree trunks and their attached foreground roots/boughs that frame the left and right edges, including the thick arching top-left trunk and top-right edge trunk and bottom corner root masses. BLACK for EVERYTHING ELSE: the central distant giant tree, water, ruins, hanging distant vines, sky/light, all scenery seen through the frame. Precisely trace the existing inner silhouettes; do not invent branches, do not alter position or scale, do not close the central opening. Solid white interior of the selected foreground silhouettes and solid black background, fine antialiased boundary only. No gray shading, no texture, no labels, no checkerboard, no transparency simulation. This mask will restore the existing foreground tree pixels over separately animated foliage, not redraw trees.

sources.description: Opaque moss-crowned ruined-stone bank texture in the master's style (2172x724), for the floor face.
sources.tool: Codex built-in image generation (style reference: the master)
sources.prompt: Use case: style-transfer, game environment material texture. Input image is a style reference; derive ONLY the ground bank material along the bottom of this forest sanctuary, not the landscape. Deliver one wide rectangular FULLY OPAQUE texture filling the entire image edge to edge, aspect ratio 3:1. Straight-on side elevation of an ancient dark forest-green ruined stone retaining bank. The uppermost edge is a continuous horizontal walkable moss crown: a thin broken yellow-green sunlit rim and dense small moss leaves, occupying the top 10 percent. Below it is substantial dark desaturated green irregular stone masonry, root tracery, chipped joints, localized creeping moss, dappled painterly texture in the same hand-painted visual family as the reference. Descend to very dark green earth and root-shadow in the bottom quarter. Texture scale: many modest stones, not three giant boulders. The left/right sides should join as a repeatable horizontal strip with no endcaps, no vertical border and no directional lighting gradient. No visible sky, water, landscape, trees, transparent margins, black external background, floating platform, text, diagram, checkerboard or separate swatches. No cyan bevel, no neon outline. This is the game ground's solid face texture, not a new scene painting. Keep fully opaque RGB across the entire rectangle.

sources.description: Segmentation of the pool (1672x941, white = water, including the reflections in it; standing stone, banks and trunks black). Its rows above the waterline wrongly mark misty openings as water, so the recipe uses it only from the waterline down.
sources.tool: Codex built-in image editor (segmentation edit of an earlier mask, with the clean plate as reference)
sources.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the WRONG black/white water mask to correct; image 2 is the exact sanctuary backing reference. Return ONLY the corrected 1672x941 black/white mask, same registration. Target the HORIZONTAL FOREGROUND POOL ONLY, roughly lower third of the scene. Make EVERY pixel above y=610 BLACK, including sky seen through upper arches. All vertical waterfalls must be BLACK. In the lower pool, make the liquid surface solid WHITE INCLUDING ALL dark wavy/reflected pillar and tree shapes: reflections are liquid, not pillars. Keep ONLY actual solid stone pillars/ruin blocks, actual foreground banks/roots and actual tree trunks BLACK; their reflections directly below their real waterline must be WHITE. The wrong mask's dangling black wavy pillar-reflection spikes around x270,y730; x425,y720; x625,y730; x820,y710; x995,y720; x1320,y740; x1460,y750 must be removed (filled WHITE), while the actual solid pillars immediately above remain BLACK. No outlines around black regions; no fine white lines on dry ruins. Preserve exact boundaries of the lower foreground pool and its real occluding architecture. The upper 610 rows are solid black by design: we will address far water separately. Pure black and white, no texture/shading/text.
